thread:
sanjay: quick recap from this morning's micro-bringup for the new 9b candidate (polaris-lite). posting raw numbers we agreed to track. TL;DR: int4 saves ~38% unit cost vs fp16, int8 ~22%. int4 shows a small quality delta on longform QA (~1.8% absolute F1 drop on our longform slice). decide whether product impact is acceptable before routing change.

bench-bot: bench run complete for polaris-lite. summary: throughput 240 tok/s (p4d), median latency 110ms @ 1-2k seq. cost-per-1k-tokens: fp16 $0.052, int8 $0.040, int4 $0.032. sample-size: 12k queries. attached metrics: top1-f1: fp16 78.6, int8 78.0, int4 76.8.

maria: putting product context — the longform F1 drop maps to ~2.5% lower satisfaction on the Summarize flow in our GTN sample. that's borderline. we need an A/B to measure downstream retention impact before wide rollout.

liz: can we hybrid route? short convs (<=256 tokens) -> int4, longform -> int8 or fp16 fallback for safety. should preserve cost savings while protecting longform quality.

own: +1 to hybrid. rough calc: if 60% of tokens are short, blended cost becomes ~int4*0.6+int8*0.4 = ~$0.0346 per 1k (vs fp16 $0.052) => ~33% savings overall. i can script routing rule.

sanjay: owen pls add a quick simulation that replays production seq_len histogram against new routing thresholds, output expected token-weighted cost and expected delta on F1. target: show cost delta and quality risk per 100k requests.

own: will do. quick plan: run 24h replay, produce CSV with columns "seq_len, token_count, route, expected_cost, quality_delta_est". sending PR to ops repo.

liz: question — how confident are we the int4 F1 drop is not due to priming? bench looked at headroom with longer KV cache?

bench-bot: ran ablation: increasing context priming reduced int4 delta by ~0.4 pts on longform (now int4 77.2). still ~1.4 pts below fp16. config used: top_k=40, temp=0.0, kv_cache warmstart enabled.

maria: product ask: can we define an explicit rollback metric? propose: if longform user satisfaction drops >1.0% absolute in canary window (7 days, 20k samples) -> rollback. also stopgap: route fallback for queries with hallucination signals (low factuality score).

sanjay: agreed. adding rollout checklist: 1) 5% canary 7d 2) monitoring: token-weighted cost (real-time), longform F1 proxy, user satisfaction metric, hallucination alarms 3) rollback triggers as maria suggested.

liz: also add a per-model "confidence score" computed from slice delta; if confidence < 0.85, restrict to offline batch jobs only.

own: replay done (first pass). quick numbers: with routing threshold 256, expected cost = $0.035/1k tokens (approx), predicted longform F1 drop (weighted) 0.6 pts (because long queries stay on int8/fp16). attaching csv to PR.

maria: that looks promising. next step: product signoff for canary and set guardrail SLOs. @sanjay can you schedule a 30m sync with infra/ops to confirm canary infra?

sanjay: scheduled 30m for tomorrow 10:30 PT, invite sent. i'll also open the canary ticket and include rollback runbooks.

liz: one more item — can we run an int4 calibration sweep for only the longform slice (temp, top_k, few-shot prompts) to try to recover the last 1pt? might be cheaper than locking longform to int8.

bench-bot: queued calibration sweep: params: top_k [20,40,60], temp [0.0,0.2], 0/1/3 shots. will post results in thread when done. ETA 18h.

owen: if calibration recovers >=0.8 pts we can push 10% traffic and iterate. otherwise fall back to hybrid routing.

maria: thanks team. summary action items: owen -> finalize routing PR + replay artifacts; bench-bot -> calibration sweep; sanjay -> canary ticket + infra sync; liz -> gating thresholds and confidence rule. will reconvene after bench results. :thumbsup:

sanjay: noted, added to tracker. closing thread for now, will post canary link here when ready.
